title: Scene Set
description:
The real Foundry Scenes this campaign ships: one landing scene, one per beat of the story, the sub-locations inside a beat, and the campaign map they are all reached from. Generated into a live world by scripts/foundry/scene-build.mjs, idempotently and by deterministic id, exactly like the audio playlists -- so a scene is authored HERE and rebuilt there, never hand-made in the world where it cannot be rebuilt or reviewed.

Replaces stage-demo.json, which built four demonstration scenes with a placeholder cast. Those were the proof that theatre-of-the-mind staging worked; these are the real thing, and they carry the same `stage` capability.

artRoot.description: Module-relative directory holding the WebP derivatives every scene's `art` names. The masters live in artwork/ and are registered in asset-registry.json; these are regenerable derivatives, not assignments.

id.description: Stable authoring id. The Foundry document id is derived from it (core/ids.mjs#deriveFoundryId), so renaming this orphans the built scene -- rename the `name`, not this.

art.description: Filename stem under artRoot, without extension. The generator appends .webp.

kind.description: landing: where a player who logs in with nothing else active lands. beat: one section of the story. sub: a room inside a beat, cut to from the Scene Runner rather than navigated to. hub: the campaign map. place: a location that exists but is not a beat of this session.

navigation.description: Whether it appears in Foundry's own scene navigation bar. Sub-scenes default to false -- twelve tabs of sub-rooms buries the six that matter.

briefRef.description: The scene-brief id this scene serves (data/scene-briefs/). What lets the Scene Runner and this scene find each other, and what ties a soundscape to a picture: both are keyed by the same brief id.

locationRef.description: The gazetteer location this happens at (data/locations/). The campaign map's pin for this scene is placed from that location's own derived.centroidPx -- never from a coordinate copied into this file, so a location that moves takes its pin with it.

locationNote.description: Set when locationRef is a PROPOSED correspondence rather than an exact one, saying so plainly. A guess recorded as a fact is how a map stops being trustworthy.

blurb.description: PLAYER-FACING. What the map pin's journal says about this place. Written from what a newcomer could actually know -- never what is waiting for them there.

mapScale.description: hub only. Multiply a campaign-map master pixel (data/map/campaign-map.json, 12400 square) by this to get a pixel in this scene. The shipped map art is the 6200px half-scale derivative, so 0.5.

pins.description: hub only. One per scene reachable from the map.

sceneRef.description: A scenes[].id -- the scene this pin travels to.

label.description: Overrides the target scene's name on the map.

offsetPx.description: Nudge, in THIS scene's pixels, applied after the location's centroid. Two real buildings eleven pixels apart need their signposts further apart than they are; the pin is a signpost, not a survey mark.
